```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", error = FALSE)
old_options <- options(width = 90)
saved_logfile <- loggit2::get_logfile()
saved_level <- loggit2::set_log_level("DEBUG", confirm = FALSE)
saved_echo <- loggit2::get_echo()
saved_calls <- loggit2::set_call_options(confirm = FALSE)
```

You can use `loggit2` without configuring it. Change a setting when you need a
persistent log, less detail, different console output or call information.

## Settings at a glance

| Setting | Default | Environment variable | Session setter / getter | Per-call argument |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Log file | `loggit.log` in `tempdir()` | `FILE_LOGGIT2` | `set_logfile()` / `get_logfile()` | `logfile` in `loggit()` and `with_loggit()` |
| Level | `"DEBUG"` | `LEVEL_LOGGIT2` | `set_log_level()` / `get_log_level()` | `log_level` in `with_loggit()`; see overrides below |
| JSON echo to stdout | `TRUE` | `ECHO_LOGGIT2` | `set_echo()` / `get_echo()` | `echo` in logging functions and condition wrappers |
| Timestamp format | `"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z"` | `TIMESTAMP_LOGGIT2` | `set_timestamp_format()` / `get_timestamp_format()` | None |
| Condition call / full stack | Both `FALSE` | None | `set_call_options()` / `get_call_options()` | No per-call replacement for these settings |

Setter functions return the previous setting invisibly, so you can restore it.
Use `confirm = FALSE` to omit the setter's confirmation message.

## Environment, session and individual calls

Environment variables initialize the session settings **when the package is
loaded**. For example, set these before the first use of `loggit2` in a fresh
R process:

```{r environment, eval = FALSE}
Sys.setenv(
  FILE_LOGGIT2 = "/existing/log/directory/application.ndjson",
  LEVEL_LOGGIT2 = "INFO",
  ECHO_LOGGIT2 = "FALSE"
)
library(loggit2)
```

Changing an environment variable after the package is loaded does not update the
current setting. Use a setter for that session. A supported per-call argument
overrides the session default for that call.

For code that others will call, prefer per-call arguments where available.
Session settings also affect `loggit2` calls made by other code in that R process.

## Choose a log file

Use a path in an existing directory. This example uses two temporary files to
keep it safe to run:

```{r log-files}
logfile <- tempfile(fileext = ".ndjson")
other_logfile <- tempfile(fileext = ".ndjson")
previous_logfile <- loggit2::set_logfile(logfile, confirm = FALSE)

loggit2::loggit("INFO", "Uses the session log", echo = FALSE)
loggit2::loggit("INFO", "Uses another log", logfile = other_logfile, echo = FALSE)

loggit2::get_logfile() == normalizePath(logfile, winslash = "/")
```

The condition wrappers, such as `loggit2::warning()`, use the session log file;
they do not have a `logfile` argument. `set_logfile()` creates the file by default
and attempts to normalize its path. Pass `NULL` to select the temporary default.

## Filter by level

The standard levels, from most to least detailed, are `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARN`,
`ERROR` and `NONE`. An `INFO` setting keeps INFO, WARN and ERROR entries.
`get_log_level()` returns the corresponding integer: DEBUG is 4 and NONE is 0.

```{r levels}
previous_level <- loggit2::set_log_level("INFO", confirm = FALSE)
loggit2::loggit("DEBUG", "This entry is filtered out", echo = FALSE)
loggit2::loggit("INFO", "This entry is kept", echo = FALSE)
loggit2::set_log_level(previous_level, confirm = FALSE)
```

Filtering the log does not suppress the underlying condition. For example, a
warning still warns when the log level is `ERROR` or `NONE`.

Use an override when a specific event must be included or omitted:

```{r overrides}
loggit2::loggit(
  "DEBUG", "Always record this event",
  ignore_log_level = TRUE, echo = FALSE
)
loggit2::message("Shown, but not written to the log", .loggit = FALSE)
```

For condition wrappers and `debuginfo()`, `.loggit = NA` follows the current
level, `TRUE` forces logging and `FALSE` disables it. Custom levels are enabled
with `loggit(..., custom_log_lvl = TRUE)` and are not filtered by the standard
level ordering.

## Control the extra JSON output

`echo` controls whether a log entry is also written as JSON to stdout. It does
not control file logging or R's normal condition handling.

```{r echo}
previous_echo <- loggit2::set_echo(FALSE, confirm = FALSE)
loggit2::message("Still logged, and still displayed as an R message")
loggit2::set_echo(previous_echo, confirm = FALSE)
```

Use `echo = FALSE` on a single call for the same effect. Use normal R condition
handlers to suppress or handle a message or warning; see
[logging existing code](logging-existing-code.html#handle-errors-without-losing-the-log).

## Understand the scope of with_loggit()

`with_loggit()` configures its own condition handlers for the expression:

```{r local-capture}
loggit2::with_loggit({
  base::message("Captured in the other log")
}, logfile = other_logfile, log_level = "INFO", echo = FALSE)
```

It does **not** change the session defaults used by a direct `loggit()` or a
condition wrapper inside the expression:

```{r scope-boundary}
loggit2::with_loggit({
  loggit2::loggit("INFO", "This still uses the session log", echo = FALSE)
}, logfile = other_logfile, log_level = "ERROR", echo = FALSE)
```

That direct event goes to `logfile`, not `other_logfile`, and uses the session
level. Avoid wrapping `loggit2` condition wrappers in `with_loggit()` for the same
condition, since both can log it.

## Include calls and timestamps

Enable call logging to help locate a condition or a debug event:

```{r calls}
previous_calls <- loggit2::set_call_options(
  log_call = TRUE, full_stack = FALSE, confirm = FALSE
)
loggit2::get_call_options()
loggit2::set_call_options(.arg_list = previous_calls, confirm = FALSE)
```

Use `full_stack = TRUE` together with `log_call = TRUE` for stack information.
Each setter call resets omitted call options to their defaults. Direct
`loggit()` events do not infer a condition call. See the
[debugging example](logging-existing-code.html#find-the-origin-of-an-event).

`set_timestamp_format()` changes the formatting used by `format(Sys.time())`.
It does not set the timezone; the host's time configuration is used.

## Restore session settings in reusable code

If per-call arguments are insufficient, restore any session settings you change.
Inside a function, register the restoration with `on.exit()`:

```{r restore-settings}
inspect_input <- function() {
  old <- loggit2::set_log_level("DEBUG", confirm = FALSE)
  on.exit(loggit2::set_log_level(old, confirm = FALSE), add = TRUE)
  loggit2::debuginfo("Inspecting input", echo = FALSE)
  120L
}

inspect_input()
```

This restores the setting even if the function exits with an error. Return to
[Getting Started](loggit2.html) for the shortest working examples.

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE}
loggit2::set_logfile(saved_logfile, confirm = FALSE, create = FALSE)
loggit2::set_log_level(saved_level, confirm = FALSE)
loggit2::set_echo(saved_echo, confirm = FALSE)
loggit2::set_call_options(.arg_list = saved_calls, confirm = FALSE)
options(old_options)
unlink(c(logfile, other_logfile))
```
